home.title: idopNetwork Web
home.hero.figure.alt: Multi-layer network diagram with M1, M2 and M3 nodes and directed edges
home.hero.intro: idopNetwork is a complex-systems framework built on the statistical mechanics proposed by Prof. Rongling Wu. Mapping static observations into a high-dimensional topological space lets us reconstruct the internal workings of a system beyond the limits of conventional statistics.
home.module.curve_fitting.title: Curve Fitting
home.module.curve_fitting.desc: Converts static data into quasi-dynamic power-law curves via niche theory and allometric growth, providing the mathematical base for the differential equations that follow.
home.module.funclu.title: FunClu
home.module.funclu.desc: Clusters traits into functional modules with a multivariate Gaussian mixture model, reducing the complexity of high-dimensional network reconstruction.
home.module.netrecon.title: NetRecon
home.module.netrecon.desc: Builds differential equations from evolutionary game theory and solves self- and interaction effects with constrained multi-task sparse regression, reconstructing a dynamic personalized network.
home.module.netanal.title: NetAnal
home.module.netanal.desc: Uses GLMY path homology to dissect the high-order structure of dynamic networks, tracking connected components, cycles and cavities across filtration thresholds.
home.profile.name: Prof. Rongling Wu
home.footer: Beijing Key Laboratory of Topological Statistics and Applications for Complex Systems · Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications · idopNetwork v2.0
home.badge.informative.tip: Turns complex data into interpretable biological or physical logic
home.badge.dynamic.tip: Captures how a system evolves over time and environments
home.badge.omnidirectional.tip: Covers interaction networks from molecules to phenotypes

fitting.title: Curve Fitting
fitting.desc: Upload one or more CSV files to turn static observations into quasi-dynamic power-law curves, or denoise time series with SWT.
fitting.uploadHint: Click or drag CSV files here
fitting.uploadHelp: The first column of each CSV is the index; the remaining columns are numeric features. The file name becomes the condition name. Multiple files are supported.
fitting.modeHint.quasi: Static observations → row-sum ordering → power-law fit y = a·x^b.
fitting.modeHint.dynamic: Time series → per-channel stationary wavelet (SWT) soft-threshold denoising.

fitting.runCreated: Run created; opening the run page
fitting.tip: Files are uploaded automatically and a background run is created; figures, tables, and the export ZIP appear on the run page.

funclu.title: Functional Clustering (FunClu)
funclu.desc: Cluster shared features across conditions with an EM Gaussian mixture fitted to the observations (quasi_dynamic) of a Curve Fitting export. The sampled power curves (curve_sample) are not clustered; they are only used for the export and the cluster profile figure.

funclu.runCreated: Run created; opening the run page
funclu.k.tip: The engine is Fast-Funclu with a power mean on the supplied scale and additive SAD(1) residuals, fitted to the observations (quasi_dynamic). S1 covariance and log_c_beta initialization are the defaults; non-positive responses fall back to KMeans. The FunClu-K ZIP feeds multi-layer network reconstruction.
funclu.bic.tip: The engine is Fast-Funclu with a power mean on the supplied scale and additive SAD(1) residuals, fitted to the observations (quasi_dynamic). Scans the joint grid of K and the selected covariance structures (S1 by default; S1–S4 can be selected); each candidate keeps the highest-likelihood run over n_init starts. The recommended model is the lowest BIC among candidates meeting the minimum module size, and the table reports AIC, ΔBIC, selected and the structure. A running scan can be cancelled at each K boundary.
